heading: Review a property strategy at both the asset and owner levels
body:
A rental-property tax question usually has two layers. The first concerns the property: cost, use, improvements, financing, depreciation history, and sale plans. The second concerns the owner: ownership structure, other income, participation, carryforwards, and applicable limitations. Resolving one layer does not automatically resolve the other.

Consider an owner evaluating a study for one building while planning to sell another. The adviser needs the existing asset schedules and expected sale timeline, not just the new study estimate. A larger deduction in one year may affect future planning, and a projected deduction is different from cash savings the owner can currently use.

Prepare a property-by-property schedule showing acquisition date, supported basis, placed-in-service facts, current use, major work, debt, and intended exit. Identify missing records instead of filling gaps with rough values that appear precise. Ask who will reconcile the property analysis to the return and which owner-level questions still require review.

Use IRS Publication 946 and the applicable year’s guidance as references. A useful engagement connects the property records, the owner’s tax position, implementation, and future changes; it does not stop at a headline deduction estimate.
